Julian Gollop's Chaos Reborn magically escapes early access

Anyone play this? I, ahem, found a demo last night and played through the first 25% of the tutorial or so (which still took about an hour).

The premise is interesting, it's kind of like Magic The Gathering with a gameboard and no mana, and everything has one HP. You summon creatures to fight for you, weapons and such to arm yourself, and have attack spells and utility spells that have various uses. Most of the spells have relatively low chances of success (30% to 50% ish), but this chance can be increased by casting other spells (there is a law/chaos meter that gives a bonus/malus to casting law/chaos spells), or you can summon creatures with 100% of success by summoning them as illusions, with the caveat being your opponent can destroy these instantly if he guesses they are illusions by 'disbelieving.' This last mechanic is really the most original part of the game, as far as I can tell.

I'm a huge fan of most of Gollop's work, I've been playing XCOM since 1994 and I even played some of his more obscure stuff like Ghost Recon Shadow Wars (which is pretty good) for the 3DS. Chaos Reborn... didn't blow me away and I probably won't play it past the tutorial/challenges, for a simple reason: there is no single player campaign.

As a MP experience it will probably be fun for the people that like that kinda thing, but I'm not one of them, I prefer games like Original Sin or Renowned Explorers (or, indeed, the XCOM series), a focus on MP turns me off entirely.

So, long story short, if you want the next great SP TBS keep looking, there's maybe 3 hrs of content here by playing the tutorials and challenges. I have no comment on the MP, it wouldn't be right.
